findings.title: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) looks up resource by client.getId() but resources are stored under the client's internal ID, and the fallback NPEs when no all-clients resource exists
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the per-client resource is looked up with resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates client resources with the name returned by resolveClient(), which is client.getId() (the internal UUID), so this lookup is consistent with creation. The real bug is the fallback path: when the per-client resource is null, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource() returns null when the 'Clients' all-resource does not exist (e.g., the admin permissions client was created before this schema change, or the resource was deleted), causing a NullPointerException instead of returning false. This turns a normal 'no permission' case into a 500 error for every admin API call that checks a client-scoped permission (canManage/canView/canConfigure/canMapRoles on a specific client).

findings.title: Fallback to all-clients resource checks policies on the wrong resource when a per-client resource exists but has no matching permission
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when a per-client resource exists (resource != null), the method evaluates permissions only on that single resource and never falls back to the 'Clients' all-resource-type resource. This is inconsistent with the Users V2 implementation and with the documented semantics ('Also if the caller has a permission to ... all clients' in ClientPermissionEvaluator javadoc). Consequence: an admin granted 'manage' on the 'Clients' resource type (all clients) will be denied manage on any specific client that happens to have a per-client resource created (e.g., because another admin previously created a permission for that client), even though the all-clients permission should grant access. The fallback is only consulted when the per-client resource is entirely absent, so behavior depends on whether an unrelated per-client resource exists — a data-integrity/authorization-correctness bug.
